Viewers step up

By: Laura Byrne | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Our stories often tell tales of people in dire straits, but this December, a few viewers stepped up to give a helping hand to their fellow South Africans

Unique Selling Point:
Our December line-up included stories of inspiring South Africans getting involved in their communities - and it looks like it inspired our viewers to do the same! We've had a stream of generous responses to our recent stories, as viewers have stepped forward to lend a helping hand.

Summary:
1. Vuvuzela Men
Russell Jones, a military veteran who owns and runs a private defence and home security business, has offered to provide Isaac and his Vuvuzela Men with basic self-defence and close protection techniques to allow them to better protect themselves and their community as they escort commuters through the twilight streets of Soweto.
One other viewer has also offered to make a monetary donation to Isaac and his guys.

2. Old folks Give Back
Sylvia Fulton has offered a large donation of wool for Mavis Frew, to help with her teddy-bear knitting. Another viewer, Sharon Evans, has donated a punching bag and boxing gloves to Sheraaz and says she hopes it will inspire other viewers to donate.

3. Kevin Kimwelle
Robert Nettl, a PE optometrist, has offered to provide a free eye test to Selina, the old lady for whom Kevin is building a house. He says he will facilitate any further treatment such as cataract surgery, that she might need.

4. School Sports Tours Scam
Two viewers donated a total of R7000 to Cynthia Mpofu, the domestic worker who lost so much money to Vision Sports. One is Karen Potgieter, a PE resident who donated R4000. The other donor wishes to remain anonymous.

Further information:
1. Vuvuzela Men
The training is scheduled to take place on Thursday 16 January 2020 at 12:00. We will accompany Russell and film him training Isaac and the guys, as well as getting some upsounds from Isaac and Russell.

2. Old folks giving back
Annalise has been in touch with Sylvia and Sharon and is organising the delivery of donated items. She will film short upsounds with both recipients about the impact it will have for them.

3. Kevin Kimwelle
Kevin is facilitating contact between Selina and Mr Nettl. Selina is due to come into the practice on 23 Janaury for her eye test. We are hoping they can film some video of it on cellphone and will follow up to find out if she will receive further treatment. Kevin is also still building Selina's house so we may postpone this update until it is complete - he is documenting the process.

4. School Sports Tours
Karen has agreed to try and film a short piece to her phone and send it to us, as she lives in PE. Cynthia has agreed to a short interview to talk about the impact of the donation on her. We will also provide a quick scripted update about the status of the investigation.

NOTE: I am still waiting for further information from Lezanne and Tarryn Crossman regarding other generous responses from viewers over the past year, which may change this proposed outline.

Press Release:


Carte Blanche Viewers Step Up
Over the holidays we set out to tell you stories about regular South Africans going beyond the call of duty to uplift their communities in big or small ways. We wanted to celebrate the best of human nature. We never expected to get such a warm and generous response from our loyal Carte Blanche viewers, who stepped in with offers of assistance, from equipment to hard cash. Some wanted to remain anonymous – but we persuaded others to share their motivation with us and see the difference their love and support has made.
Producer: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


UPSOUND: Cynthia Mpofu: What I went through, it was really a trauma, and I didn’t expect that there could be anyone who could reach out.
VO1: Last year Carte Blanche investigated a school sports tour operator gone rogue, and met the parents left out of pocket and reeling. Cynthia Mpofu was one of them, losing over R37 000 when Vision Sports cancelled her son Anthony’s Netherlands hockey tour.
UPSOUND: Karen Potgieter: This mom, who was already battling to put her son through school, and already had to apply for bursaries to do just that, had given of her all and had done her utmost to provide this sports trip for him. And to have that taken away from her, as a mom it was incredibly heart-breaking to watch.
VO: Cynthia’s story touched your hearts. One anonymous viewer donated R3000. Karen Potgieter gifted her a further R4000.
UPSOUND: Karen Potgieter: I really just wanted to replace some of the hope that Cynthia had lost through this story and I feel that if we are ever in a position to help another, we must really take the opportunity to do that.
UPSOUND: Cynthia Mpofu: Even a word, for someone giving you a word of encouragement and a word of strength. It means a lot. Because life is not about money. But life is about love and caring and encouraging each other.
LINK: Carte Blanche is a show known for its exposés of seedy scamsters and political crooks…it’s not every day that we get to do a story about ordinary people reaching out to make their neighbours’ lives better.
VO: But in December, we set out to find those South Africans and bring you their stories.
UPSOUND: Sharon Evans: I saw the programme on Carte Blanche about the good work that Mr Sheraaz is doing and we had this bag, it was lying around, nobody was using it and we thought, it can definitely be put to good use here.
VO: Sharon was inspired to donate her unused sports equipment to Sheraaz Maarman who runs a boxing school in Bishop Lavis, Cape Town.
UPSOUND: Sheraaz Maarman: 2020 is starting very good with the help of the donation we got today and we hope that it’s not the last donation.
LINK: Our story about pensioners giving back to their communities proved that you don’t have to have a lot to make a meaningful change in somebody else’s life. And you, our Carte Blanche viewers, got the message because you decided to step up and pay it forward.
VO: Veteran knitter Mavis Frew lovingly crafts beanies and teddy bears for abused children. Sylvia Fulton came forward with a large donation of wool.
UPSOUND: Sylvia Fulton: All for Auntie Mavis, may she be blessed.
UPSOUND: Mavis: Isn’t this lovely? Oh, I’m so blessed. What do I do to deserve this?
UPSOUND: Sylvia: I stand by her side with her cause and I really appreciate her.
UPSOUND: Mavis: I’m gobsmacked with all this wool. Ooh! I’m going to have a wonderful time.
VO: Around the country, you offered what you had, whether it was funds, goods or skills. One viewer was moved by our story about Isaac Makhuba and his Vuvuzela Men, who patrol Soweto’s streets armed with nothing more than vuvuzelas and sticks.
LINK: We’re here in Soweto to meet Russell Jones, who’s planning to give Isaac a competitive edge in his mission to protect residents from crime on their daily commute.
UPSOUND: Russell: In the more affluent areas, your neighbourhood watches typically have bullet-proof vests, they have guns, they have torches, they have batons. These guys are a lot more at risk with a lot less equipment. It’s very brave, and they’ve got my respect, my utmost respect.
VO: Russell is the founder of a company providing personal security education and products. He has brought the guys a donation of pepper spray and is teaching them how to respond to an attack.
UPSOUND: Isaac: He teaches us well how to respond when a thug on the street has a gun with them, how do we approach that situation and how to save someone else.
UPSOUND: Russell: Keep practising, let’s do a few more times. You’ve got to be comfortable with this.
UPSOUND: Sisi: My training went very well; it was great because I had a lot to learn.
VO: It doesn’t stop here. Russell has pledged to donate a portion of his online sales towards equipment for the Vuvuzela Men.
UPSOUND: Isaac: Before we received this training we have encountered situations where we were held at gunpoint. I myself have been a victim of such a situation, but there was nothing I could do. I didn’t know then how to handle it because I hadn’t received this kind of training.
UPSOUND: Russell: This is something in a worst case scenario that they can use to save their lives or to save someone else’s life.
VO: Whether it’s saving a life or running a soup kitchen out of their own pockets, these people do what they do out of love. And with your help, they’ve been seen.
UPSOUND: Cynthia Mpofu: That shows Ubuntu to say if you’ve got a problem or a challenge, don’t think you are alone.
UPSOUND: Mavis Frew: If everybody just lifted their hands and they helped one person, life would be better for all of us.

PROMOS

1. In December, we celebrated ordinary people doing something extraordinary for their fellow South Africans. Imagine our delight when you, our viewers, were inspired to step up too and do your part!

2. From assistance with equipment to hard cash, our generous Carte Blanche viewers have stepped up to assist some of the remarkable South Africans we featured in our Christmas shows.

3. Our December stories showed extraordinary people giving the little they have to improve their neighbours’ lives. And you, our Carte Blanche viewers, got the message because you decided to step up too and pay it forward.
